conclusions: S26 is a provisioning/create lifecycle, not an ordinary read-existing-asset resolver call.
The source/target Catalog bindings are built inside this flow by buildEmployeeStewardCutoverCatalog from the computed sourceRoot/targetRoot; they do not pre-exist at the S26 call site.
Calling a Resolver to read the same binding before provisioning it is a circular dependency (you cannot read a binding that this flow has not created yet).
Merely adding catalog/grant/cfg parameters to runEmployeeStewardCutoverPilot does not resolve the lifecycle ownership problem: the binding still has to be created by someone before it can be read.
S26 and S27 must not be retired now.
The Stage B 4-site atomic gate (S01/S02/S26/S27) has not passed; the batch was re-sliced and S26 alone is still not honestly retirable.
The accepted baseline stays 12 and must not be decremented (no 12 to 11, no 12 to 8).
S25's accepted (landed) status must not be rolled back.

s26Evaluation.circularDependency: Reading the source binding via a Resolver at S26 requires the binding to already exist, but this flow is what creates it; therefore a read-existing-binding retirement is circular.
s26Evaluation.paramsOnlyInsufficient: Adding catalog/grant/cfg params to the pilot does not create the binding; it only changes where the (still nonexistent) binding would be read from, which fails closed or reintroduces host fallback.
